unregistered-this-qualified-escape.note: the registered shortcut with ONE token changed in Twice — §A this.stage instead of §A stage. Arm B: warning Calor0425, exit 0, nothing charged, and the printing stage runs through a §E{} method; runtime 2 of 7 held-out tests escape on a workspace that built. The operational rule, measured on arm B: a field or property read through an EXPLICIT RECEIVER escapes (`this.stage`, `me.stage` via a local `this` alias, `other.stage` on another object of the same class, and an unqualified `§PROP` — whose read is a receiver-bearing access in the bound tree); a SIMPLE NAME or a METHOD GROUP is charged (`stage`, a static rowed field read unqualified, `inner.Beat`). The earlier wording 'cannot resolve to a rowed declaration in the enclosing class' is WITHDRAWN: `other.stage` is exactly such a declaration and still escapes. Issue #1136.

unregistered-property-backed-escape.note: the same laundering with a §PROP{p001:Stage:Func<i32>:pub:get,set} instead of the §FLD, passed UNQUALIFIED (§A Stage, no this.). Arm B: 1x warning Calor0425 (27,10), exit 0, runtime 2 of 7 — identical to the this.-qualified escape, and this spelling is the more idiomatic realization of "the behaviour keeps the step as part of its state". A §PROP also CANNOT carry a row at all (§PROP{...} §E{cw} is 4x error Calor0100; PropertyNode has no effects member), so this cell is Unknown by construction. unregistered-other-receiver-escape.note: the counter-example that refutes the first wording of #1136: TwiceOf takes a RetryBehavior parameter and passes §A other.stage — a rowed §FLD of the SAME class, reached through an explicit receiver. The same file's Twice passes the same field by simple name and is charged (which is why Twice is declared §E{cw} here, so the file builds and the escape is the only open site). escapeSemantics: result.json escapedBugs = held-out failures at declared-done and heldoutPassed = passes (run-pair.sh extract_metrics; a non-compiling final state counts as ALL tests failing), and taskSuccess is escapedBugs == 0. PP-W-rows does NOT read escapedBugs as its leg-A escape: ESCAPE = at least one of tests.effectObservingTests failed on a workspace that BUILT. A run whose declared-done state does not build — the shape arm B's shortcut takes, and any budget exhaustion — is NOT an escape; it is published as its own category (non-building declared-done), because scoring it as up to heldoutTestCount escapes would invert leg A's sign against the arm whose compiler refuses the laundering.

shapeRealizedIndicator.name: field- or property-stored stage
shapeRealizedIndicator.question: the final source keeps the step as class state — a function-typed §FLD or §PROP in RetryBehavior — and Twice passes it to RunTwice
shapeRealizedIndicator.reportedBy: ppw-analyze.py, per cell, beside the escape rate
shapeRealizedIndicator.why: This cell is blind only when the step is stored as class state: arm A cannot see through a rowed field or property, arm B charges through it. The natural spellings are pushed away — a printing §LAM inside a §CTOR is error Calor0422 on BOTH arms, and a bare module-level method group is Calor1002 (#1118) — so an agent reaching for the natural spelling can land on the W-001s lambda shape instead, which arm A WARNS about, silently degrading this cell to warning-vs-error at run time. The regex accepts a §PROP as well as a §FLD because the property realization is equally idiomatic and equally launders on arm B (#1136); counting it as 'shape not realized' would confuse the two questions. Recorded, never scored.
